subject: Making package easily available across OSs

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Making package easily available across OSs
parts:
Hi,
Thanks to devtools, I have developed my fiirst package: A library of helpers for doing SEM with OpenMx

https://github.com/tbates/umx

It's running well for me, and for install_github(tbates/umx) users on mac.

Just had my first PC user... they just can't get it to run.

It's just source R files, with roxygen help. No C/Fortran etc, so, some questions:

1. How can one release binary packages at github (to avoid the need for users to have compile tools)
2. How can one create windows and *nix binary packages from a mac?
3. Why can't a PC user install packages from source when a mac user can?
4. If  one pushes a package to CRAN, is it frowned on to then push updates often?

many thanks, t

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: Making package easily available across OSs
parts:
discovered build_win()
Is there a way to bulld packages with dependencies on packages that are not on CRAN? (umx requires OpenMx, which is currently installed  from http://openmx.psyc.virginia.edu  due to a non-open source optimiser being included in the package.

Also, does install_github detect the availability of the corect binary packages? i..e, I just push them up to github?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Making package easily available across OSs
parts: > Just had my first PC user... they just can't get it to run.
Error messages?

> It's just source R files, with roxygen help. No C/Fortran etc, so, some
> questions:
>
> 1. How can one release binary packages at github (to avoid the need for
> users to have compile tools)
You can't, but it doesn't sound like you need.
> 2. How can one create windows and *nix binary packages from a mac?
You can't easily - it's hard enough that I don't think it's worth bothering.

> 4. If one pushes a package to CRAN, is it frowned on to then push updates
> often?

Yes, CRAN gets antsy if you change too often.

Hadley

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: Making package easily available across OSs
parts:
On Tuesday, November 12, 2013 12:26:41 PM UTC, Hadley Wickham wrote:
Sounds like OpenMX isn't installed for 64-bit architecture.

Yes: OpenMx is not installed for 64bit R. (a dll  it requires is not compiled for 64-bit windows).

But why does devtools require it to be? i.e., is it assuming a 64 bit install (perhaps the user's app and cmdline versions for R are discrepant?), or is it demanding that both versions be installable?

Can I give a setting somewhere to only try and install the 32 bit version?

tx, t

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: Making package easily available across OSs
parts: OK: Looks like the user must delete R64 from their system to avoid the install error when a package is not available for that platform...

tx, t

or "try install_github(..., args = "--no-multiarch")"
